newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks trade up after early fall on Deng.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks trade up after early fall on Deng.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks shook off an early decline on Thursday to move higher in morning trade after the death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping removed the uncertainty which had been plaguing prices over recent sessions.

The Hang Seng Index was up 104.29 points, or 0.80 percent, at 13,210.61 in mid-morning after opening on a loss of 92 points. Turnover was HK$2.29 billion (US$294 million) after the first half hour of trade.
China announced Deng died late on Wednesday of complications from Parkinson's disease and a lung infection.
"This is something that stock markets have been gearing up for for some considerable time," said Peter Churchouse, regional strategist at Morgan Stanley.

"People have got used to the idea and thought long and hard about likely directions in China post-Deng anyway. People have got their own views and have become more or less comfortable with them," he said.

Concerns about Deng Xiaoping's health contributed to a recent slide in Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index. From an all-time high of 14,004.93 on January 16, the blue chip barometer has tumbled 899 points to Wednesday's close of 13,106.32.
"Last week we already knew and people shorted the market, waiting to buy back after the news," said Janet Gillies, sales director at OCBC Securities.
"He (Deng) really has not been a factor in the past year," she added.
Hang Seng Index futures also traded higher on Thursday. The February contract jumped 120 points to 13,200 after falling to a low of 12,980 in early trade.
"It's nice to have the rumours of Deng's death finally out of the picture," said Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager Nikko Securities.

Alistair Candlish, sales director at W.I. Carr Derivatives, said the market may now find the momentum to push the Hang Seng Index up to 13,400 points. He expected the blue chip barometer to return to 14,000 points by the time Hong Kong returns to Chinese rule on midnight of June 30.
"This is what we have been waiting for," he said.
"We are likely to see a bit of volatility in the next few days, but I do not expect a large move," Candlish added.
The Stock Exchange of Hong Kong issued a statement saying trading was being conducted as usual.

"The Stock Exchange of Hong Kong regrets to learn of the death of Deng Xiaoping. The Exchange is monitoring the markets closely and has found that our markets have been operating in an orderly and efficient manner," it said.
Among the blue chips, Swire Pacific rose HK$1.00 to HK$65.75 and Cheung Kong advanced HK$0.75 to HK$71.75. HSBC Holdings was up HK$0.50 at HK$185.50. (US$1=HK$7.8)
